change: Removed secondary Quads entry. The leg press calf raise is a calf isolation exercise where the knee is fixed/locked at a slight bend throughout — the quadriceps provide only negligible isometric stabilization and are not meaningfully secondary. Removing Quads avoids inflation of the muscle list.

Removed secondary Quads entry for the same reason as the single-leg variant: the knee is held fixed during plantar flexion, making quadriceps engagement negligible and not warranting a secondary listing.

Added Adductors as secondary. EMG and biomechanics sources confirm the hip adductors activate meaningfully to stabilize the hip and control knee alignment during unilateral leg press. Obliques secondary retained (anti-rotation demand is real in unilateral machine press as confirmed by instructions cue 'resist twisting').
Added Adductors as secondary. Sources confirm adductors contribute to hip/knee stabilization during bilateral leg press. No other changes needed.

Swapped primary/secondary for Glutes+Hamstrings vs Quads. In a forward sled DRAG (walking forward, weight dragged behind), the hip extensors (glutes and hamstrings) are the prime movers per biomechanics references — this differs from a sled PUSH where quads dominate. Quads moved to secondary (knee extension/stabilization during stride). Added Lower Back (Erector Spinae) as secondary — core stability and upright posture under load requires meaningful erector engagement.
